decode.summary: You're moving to the Q1 forecasting project on Monday. Before then, hand off the dashboard and talk with Dana.

implicitExpectations.expectation: Leave the dashboard so someone else can pick it up: notes on what's done, what's left, and where the files are.
implicitExpectations.why: "Wrap up" when you're moving projects usually means a handoff, not finishing everything.

implicitExpectations.expectation: Reach out to Dana yourself before Monday.
implicitExpectations.why: "When you get a chance" sounds optional, but with a Monday start it means this week.

steps.text: Ask Alex for the handoff details in writing.
steps.why: Your manual says written instructions work best for you.

steps.text: Write a short handoff note for the dashboard: done, left, where files are.
Message Dana to set a 20-minute sync before Monday.
Read the forecasting project's main document.
List three questions for your first day on the new project.

transitionPlan: Today: get the handoff details in writing.
Before Friday: handoff note done and sync with Dana booked.
Monday: start with Dana's walkthrough, not on your own.
questionsToAsk: Who will own the dashboard after I move?
What should I have ready for Monday?

uncertainties.what: "When you get a chance" doesn't say when to sync with Dana.
uncertainties.suggestedQuestion: Hi Alex! Should I sync with Dana before Monday, or is early next week fine?

profileUsed.how: You prefer written instructions, so step 1 asks for the handoff in writing.
Vague timing stresses you, so Pip turned "when you get a chance" into a question.
You need the why first, so the plan starts with the handoff details.
